body: Friday, March 14 2025 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information available before 2025-03-14 00:00 UTC. Prices use completed prior sessions. Prepared retrospectively; later outcomes are excluded.

Macro Stance: US equities have slipped into correction, and the trigger is tariff policy more than the data. The S&P 500 closed at 5,521.52 index points, down 8.76% over 20 sessions and 3.78% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). CNN framed the day as the Dow sliding and the S&P 500 closing in correction as the trade war escalated [1]. Goldman Sachs cut its year-end S&P 500 target to 6,200 on weaker profit forecasts [2], while Citi kept 6,500 as its base case [3], so the sell-side split is about how much earnings damage tariffs will do, not about the direction of the tape. The growth data are softer than the prices. February CPI came in at 2.8%, under consensus [4], and payrolls rose 151,000, below expectations [5]. Powell said the Fed is in no hurry to adjust rates while policy uncertainty runs high [6]. The VIX closed at 24.66, up 55.19% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and a J.P. Morgan economist puts the US recession odds at 40% [7].

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.94% and the 10Y at 4.27% (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-13), leaving the 10Y−2Y spread at +33 bps. Over 20 observations the 2Y fell 42 bps and the 10Y fell 35 bps, so the spread widened 7 bps. The curve is positively sloped, and the 20-observation move is bull steepening, with the front end rallying harder than the long end (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-13). The 30Y sits at 4.59%, 24 bps lower over 20 observations, which is a rally led by the policy path rather than a term-premium shock. TLT is up 3.92% over 20 sessions while HYG is down 1.00%, so the bid is in duration rather than credit (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The dollar index stands at 103.83 index points, down 3.81% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the recent dollar decline a natural ‘adjustment’ [8].

New / Most Important: The most important near-term item is the funding deadline. The New York Times reports that Schumer will clear the way for the Republican spending bill, breaking with his party [9], and Senate Democrats signalled they will advance the bill to avoid a shutdown [10]. CNN put the stakes as what is at risk if Congress does not fund the government by Friday [11]. A shutdown would arrive in the same week the tariff escalation has already pushed the index into correction. CNBC’s argument that markets have learned to ignore shutdowns [12] is the bull case, but it carries less weight when tariffs are already compressing earnings expectations.

Playbook ✓: Keep duration as the hedge and do not add cyclical equity until the funding vote and the tariff talks clear. Own the long end only while the curve keeps bull steepening, and trim high-beta Nasdaq exposure until the Nasdaq 100 recovers its 20-session reference of 21,719.26 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The call changes if the VIX returns toward its level of 15.89 from 20 sessions earlier and the stopgap clears without a tariff escalation (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

Macro Stance: Europe is easing into a tariff shock with its policy rate already falling. The ECB cut its key rate to 2.5% in early March [13] and described policy as ‘meaningfully less restrictive’ [14]. The first risk is that the trade shock hits Germany: the Bundesbank chief said US tariffs could extend Germany’s recession [15]. The fiscal turn is the offset. Markets rallied when Berlin moved to lift the debt brake for defence and infrastructure [16], and the shift has been called Germany’s ‘whatever it takes’ moment [17]. JPMorgan raised its euro-area 2025 growth forecast, joining Goldman [18]. The DAX is down 0.20% over 20 sessions against 3.13% for the Euro Stoxx 50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the German core is holding up better than the bloc.

Credit & Inflation: Inflation is cooling. Euro-area inflation dipped to 2.4% in February, and the ECB bets point to a sixth rate cut [19]. Lagarde warned that trade and defence shocks risk amplifying inflation [20], and that higher defence spending could push it up [21]. France is the credit pressure point, with borrowing costs near a 14-year high before a Fitch review [22]. Bund safe-haven status is holding in swaps even as German spending worries mount [23].

New / Most Important: Trade retaliation has moved from threat to action. The EU will impose counter-tariffs on $28 billion of US goods [24], and Trump answered with a threatened 200% tariff on European wine after the EU proposed a whiskey tax [25]. The US trade representative issued a statement on the EU’s retaliatory tariffs [26]. US importers of EU wine are already warning of closures and layoffs [27].

Playbook ✓: Own German fiscal beneficiaries on dips, the infrastructure and industrial suppliers that gain from the spending plan, and keep the defence leaders as the cash-flow anchor. Avoid European autos until the tariff path is settled. The call changes if the counter-tariffs are shelved, which would lift autos, or if the Bundesbank’s warning turns into an orders downgrade, which would turn the German overweight into a trim.

Macro Stance: China is trying to hold growth near its target while deflation keeps deepening. The 5% growth goal sets the frame, and South China Morning Post opinion asks where that growth will come from [28]. The annual Congress closed with questions still open about how to revive a slowing economy [29]. The stimulus on the table is a $41 billion consumption plan, which CNBC calls just a start as deflationary pressures deepen [30]. CNN says deflation problems are getting worse [31], and Bloomberg asks why China cannot escape the cycle [32]. Policy direction is supportive, but the price data are not confirming it, so the stance is Mixed.

PMIs & Activity: The most recent activity print is February’s non-manufacturing PMI at 50.4, a reading just above the expansion line for services and construction [33]. That is a positive but thin signal, and it sits against the deflation reading. The view is confirmed if the next non-manufacturing PMI holds above 50 while consumer prices stay in deflation. A drop back below 50 would confirm the bear case that the consumption plan is too small for the demand gap. The index level, not the trend, is the signal today.

Credit Impulse: Credit is the weakest part of the picture, and the evidence is about stress rather than volume. China’s bond yields jumped to three-month highs as investors pared rate-cut expectations [34]. Evergrande and other units were ordered to repay $1.8 billion of deposit pledges [35], and some Hong Kong banks are refusing home loans for Vanke’s Le Mont project in Tai Po [36]. Higher yields with cuts priced out are the opposite of a credit impulse. The read rests on the yield move and the lender retreat, which is enough to keep the credit call negative.

Property: Property is still in adjustment, and policy is steering toward quality over volume. A State Council piece frames the new vision as quality homes amid market adjustment [37], and analysts warn that the push for better homes adds stress for developers [38]. A minister says the sector is showing positive changes [39], which is the official line. Hong Kong’s property slump is pushing hotels toward student housing [40], a sign of how long the pressure lasts. Turnover is the constraint on any rebound, and the policy direction does not change that in the near term.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Policy is leaning on trade management rather than domestic demand. China’s tariffs on US farm products took effect [41], and Beijing took issue with the US linking tariffs to fentanyl [42]. The commerce ministry met Walmart over supplier pricing [43], a domestic pricing step that shows the government is watching retailers’ costs. A summit between Trump and Xi is being discussed for June [44], which keeps a negotiation channel open. The fiscal anchor is the 5% growth goal, so the next signal is whether Beijing sizes support above the $41 billion consumption plan [30].

Markets & Flows: Equities are the bright spot. The Hang Seng closed at 23,462.65 index points, up 7.56% over 20 sessions though down 0.58% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The Shanghai Composite is at 3,358.73 index points, up 0.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Hong Kong’s market has been booming while Wall Street is in turmoil [45], and ADR premiums for Chinese names are widening as the stock rerating continues [46]. The China large-cap ETF (FXI) is up 7.08% over 20 sessions and the internet ETF (KWEB) is up 5.87% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Chinese stocks and emerging-market debt drew large inflows in February [47], and mainland investors bought a record amount of Hong Kong stocks to play AI [48]. The currency is firmer: USD/CNY closed at 7.2371, down 0.98% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and the offshore yuan climbed to a four-month high [49].

New / Most Important: The new signal is the gap between the stimulus size and the deflation problem. The $41 billion consumption plan [30] sits beside a 5% growth goal, and the market is reading it as a start rather than a fix. The equity leg is being carried by AI. Alibaba released an AI model that reads emotions to take on OpenAI [50], and its chairman Joe Tsai argues that consumers’ $20 trillion of savings is the growth lever China needs [51]. The next change to the view comes from policy. If Beijing extends consumption support beyond this plan, the deflation read improves; if it does not, the equity rally runs ahead of the economy.

Playbook ✓: Own the equity beta in Hong Kong internet and AI names on dips, keep duration neutral, and avoid property developers until the credit data confirm a turn. Keep yuan exposure small above the four-month high. The call changes if the consumption plan is extended and the PMI holds above 50. ⚠ Divergence: the Hang Seng is up 7.56% over 20 sessions while the credit and property reads are still negative (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

Macro Stance: Japan’s rate path is tightening into a weak growth patch. The 10-year yield reached its highest level since 2008 on bets for BOJ hikes [52], and Reuters reports that a rate-hike discussion could come in May if inflation risks persist [53]. Growth is softer: the economy downgraded its fourth-quarter GDP [54], and services sentiment soured on the cost of living [55]. Wages are the reason the BOJ leans hawkish. Major firms agreed large pay increases [56], and the largest union group sought its biggest wage increase in over 30 years [57]. The Nikkei 225 sits at 36,790.03 index points, down 5.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY closed at 148.2790, down 3.87% over 20 sessions, which means the yen has strengthened against the dollar (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The yen is also being bid as a haven: one strategist calls it the new safe-haven currency [58], while Kuroda warned that Japan must fix the impression that it manipulates the yen [59]. The tariff track is unhelpful. Japan’s trade minister did not win a tariff exemption assurance [60], and the prime minister’s gifts apology clouded the budget outlook [61]. Toyota is down 2.89% over 20 sessions and Sony is up 3.47% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so exporter shares are not moving as one.

Playbook ✓: Favour banks and domestic wage beneficiaries over exporters while the BOJ path is live, and use yen longs as the hedge for exporter exposure. Avoid adding long-duration JGBs at 2008-high yields until the May discussion is clearer. The call changes if the tariff talks produce a concrete exemption or if the yen reverses above its 20-session reference of 154.2550 (2025-02-13).

Macro Stance: Australia’s growth is turning up from a low base. The economy exited a 21-month per capita recession [62], and Bloomberg reports that growth accelerated, which backs the RBA’s hawkish tone [63]. The RBA cut in February [64], and the governor has played down the chance of more cuts [65]. Tariffs are the drag. Albanese called US tariffs ‘not a friendly act’ [66], and Trump has said Australia’s hope of an exemption is fading [67]. Canberra says it will not retaliate [68].

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.6328, up 0.71% over 20 sessions, so the currency is holding up despite the tariff noise (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The ASX 200 is at 7,749.10 index points, down 9.26% over 20 sessions and 4.27% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). BlackRock cut its exposure to Australian shares on value grounds [69], and the iron ore chain is under pressure from China’s steel cuts [70]. BHP is down 6.71% over 20 sessions and Fortescue 19.38% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The central bank has also raised concern about banks’ plan to shut a key payments system [71].

Playbook ✓: Hold the miners on pullbacks only while iron ore holds, underweight the banks against the ASX 200’s drawdown, and keep the AUD long as the tariff hedge. The call flips if China’s steel cuts reverse and the miners lead the index back up. A break in the Australian dollar’s own trend would change the currency view, not the equity one.

Macro Stance: The Polish economy is turning up. The manufacturing PMI signalled a recovery in industry and an end to a nearly three-year recession [72]. The central bank governor, Glapiński, said there are no reasons to cut rates now [73], and said the fall in inflation is still a ‘dość odległy horyzont’, a distant horizon [74]. The rate path is therefore a hold. Parkiet argues it is not the time for emotion around the monetary council, the RPP [75], while Business Insider Polska frames the next decision as relief for borrowers arriving [76]. The labour data conflict. Eurostat put Poland at a record-low unemployment rate, joint-lowest in the EU [77], while the labour ministry explains a rise in unemployment [78], so the labour market gets no directional call. Official wage data are positive, with GUS reporting 2024 pay figures that show higher earnings [79].

Markets: The zloty is the strongest asset in the block. USD/PLN closed at 3.8452, down 3.93% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.1838 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The euro was at its cheapest against the zloty since 2018 [80], and Bloomberg reported that the zloty surged to a 10-year high on a hawkish central bank [81]. The governor also made an unambiguous statement on whether the central bank would intervene in the currency [82]. Equities are following. The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 50.96 PLN, up 3.44% over 20 sessions, and the iShares MSCI Poland ETF at 27.58 USD, up 7.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Orlen is up 16.10% over 20 sessions and PKO 3.50% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

Fiscal & Politics: Fiscal policy is leaning toward defence. EU ministers backed a temporary exemption for defence spending from the EU’s budget rules [83], and a Credit Agricole economist says the Union is moving toward looser fiscal rules [84]. The VAT gap fell unexpectedly last year, which helps the budget arithmetic [85]. Politically, the far-right candidate has moved into second place in the presidential race [86], and Biejat, who says she would tidy up the mortgage market as president, is pitching on housing [87]. The US has said it will retaliate if Poland introduces a tax on big tech [88].

Corporate & Sectors: Corporate news is strong, and buybacks are the common thread. Allegro expects 2025 earnings growth and proposed a $364 million buyback [89], and the Polish press reports double-digit profit growth, with the company saying it has proved it can deliver [90]. Allegro closed at 32.38 PLN, up 13.61% in the prior session and 11.02% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). PKO BP’s results show Poland’s largest bank boasting a profit jump of almost 4 billion zloty [91], and a record dividend is being discussed [92]; the shares closed at 74.02 PLN, up 3.32% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Orlen still lacks a final agreement with Sołowow on the small-nuclear project [93], yet Orlen is up 16.10% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Dino Polska is hiring 1,300 people [94] and its shares are at a record high [95]. KGHM’s chief executive says years of neglect and no investment are the problem [96], and the stock is down 2.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

Geopolitics & Security: Security is the louder narrative. Polish President Duda urged the US to move nuclear warheads onto Polish territory, the FT reported [97], and told the BBC that US nuclear weapons in Poland would be a deterrent for Russia [98]. Warsaw wants 100,000 volunteers for military training in 2027 [99] and has asked NATO to raise the minimum defence spending to 3% of GDP [100]. Prosecutors say Russia used a spy posing as a Belarusian refugee to set a Warsaw mall on fire [101]. Washington’s line is blunter: Rubio told Poland to ‘say thank you’ amid the Starlink spat over Ukraine [102].

New / Most Important: The one signal that matters is that defence is now both a budget and a currency story. The EU’s temporary carve-out [83] and the 3% NATO request [100] turn defence into a multi-year fiscal commitment. Speculative equity money is following: Bankier reports that steel and armaments names have taken over speculative attention on the Warsaw exchange [103], and a separate Bankier piece says the defence sector is trading on the military rally [104]. For investors the meaning is that the Polish equity move increasingly depends on military budgets rather than on the consumer.

Playbook ✓: Own the zloty winners with dividend and buyback support, PKO and Allegro, and keep the defence names as a tactical trade rather than a core holding. Hedge a zloty long against a surprise shift in the central bank’s tone, even though the governor has ruled out reasons to cut for now. The call changes if USD/PLN climbs back above its reference of 4.0026 from 13 February (Yahoo Finance). ⚠ Divergence: the WIG20 tracker is up 3.44% over 20 sessions while KGHM is down 2.75% over the same period (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

Narrative: The consensus says AI demand keeps technology earnings compounding, while the 20-session tape says the market is repricing monetisation. The Technology Select Sector SPDR is at 207.66 USD, down 11.94% over 20 sessions and 1.90% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The driver that matters now is whether software and AI spending can show revenue, not just usage, and Reuters reports that Adobe’s dull forecast raised AI monetisation doubts [105].

Reported: Adobe beat on its first quarter, but its revenue outlook disappointed and the stock fell [106]. CNBC put the drop at 14% as concerns about AI growth overshadowed the beat [107], and Adobe is down 13.85% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Oracle’s sales missed estimates even as its chief executive pointed to AI-driven growth [108]. Workday’s full-year EPS missed expectations [109].

EPS Upside Watch: The set-up for a surprise is in AI infrastructure rather than application software. ServiceNow agreed a record $2.9 billion deal for Moveworks [110], and Broadcom’s call highlighted record revenue and AI growth [111]. Suppliers are lining up announcements for the 2025 Nvidia GTC conference [112], which gives the chain a pending showcase.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Nvidia held up better than its Magnificent Seven peers during Thursday’s rout [113], which cuts against the idea that AI leaders are de-rating in lockstep. Nvidia closed at 115.58 USD, down 11.87% over 20 sessions but up 4.53% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

Narrative: The consensus is that ad-supported platforms and streaming keep growing. The Communication Services SPDR is at 94.84 USD, down 8.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Meta is the swing name, down 18.58% over 20 sessions and 4.67% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Ad budgets are under pressure too: Sirius XM fell 8.6% as its ad sales collapsed [114].

Reported: Telecoms flagged softness, and Verizon and AT&T shares slid after both signalled near-term weakness [115]. Netflix is down 13.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Meta is launching Community Notes in the US [116], a product step rather than a reported result.

EPS Upside Watch: The upside lever is creator monetisation. Facebook now lets creators get paid for views on stories [117], which adds revenue at the margin, though it is small against the ad-budget squeeze. Spotify’s $10 billion payment to the music industry shows the royalty cost base is rising [118], which limits the streaming upside.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Telecom is the exception to the sector’s weakness. Verizon is up 7.85% and AT&T 2.88% over 20 sessions while the sector ETF is down 8.35% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the defensive bid is working inside a sector that is supposed to be growth.

Narrative: The consensus is that banks are cheap on capital return. The Financial Select SPDR is at 47.42 USD, down 7.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The driver is recession pricing and credit: US corporate bond spreads hit their widest in about six months on recession fears [119], and Goldman Sachs says spreads will get a lot wider amid tariffs [120]. JPMorgan is down 18.25% over 20 sessions and Goldman Sachs 19.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

Reported: Bank stocks tumbled as recession fears rose [121], and Citigroup, Goldman Sachs and SoFi were hit hardest in the Monday sell-off [122]. Bank of America cut 150 junior investment-banking jobs [123], a cost signal rather than a loss signal. Goldman’s 2024 results beat expectations [124], an older print that still anchors the group’s earnings base.

EPS Upside Watch: The upside case rests on cost discipline and trading. Bank of America’s cuts [123] and the Stifel regulatory fine [125] show the group trimming costs, and the volatility of the tariff tape is the usual driver of trading desks’ revenue, so a surprise would come from trading activity.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Berkshire Hathaway is up 6.89% over 20 sessions while the sector falls (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and Warren Buffett’s ‘keep your head’ advice in a falling market reached a wide audience [126]. Berkshire is acting as the shelter in this tape.

Narrative: The consensus is that OPEC+ supply and softer demand keep crude range-bound. WTI closed at 66.55 USD, down 6.75% over 20 sessions, while the energy ETF is up 1.42% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The IEA’s March oil market report is the demand reference [127], and oil settled lower on tariff worry and supply-demand expectations [128].

Reported: The sector’s corporate news is about structure rather than results. Whitecap and Veren merged, reshaping the Canadian energy landscape [129], and Shell rose while the market fell [130]. The reported move is in the share reaction, not the commodity.

EPS Upside Watch: Record OPEC+ fuel exports blunt the group’s crude supply cut [131], which caps the price upside. The upside case is in gas: Henry Hub closed at 4.11 USD, up 15.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and AI and LNG demand are expected to keep US gas use at record highs [132].

⚡ Breaking Convention: Russia’s high-flying gas exporter is crippled as Europe stays away [133], and the US has sanctioned Iran’s oil minister and the shadow fleet [134]. Those are supply-side tailwinds that crude is not showing, since WTI is down 6.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

Narrative: The consensus is that industrials lose to tariffs but win on spending. The Industrial Select SPDR is at 128.78 USD, down 6.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The tariffs are landing: the steel and aluminium tariffs took effect and set off global retaliation [135], and US physical aluminium premiums hit a record [136].

Reported: Delta cut its profit forecast on macro uncertainty [137], and its shares fell after the outlook cut [138]. Rheinmetall rose 7% on its results and the European defence boost [139], and its full-year call highlighted record growth [140].

EPS Upside Watch: Defence is the set-up. European money managers are starting to bring defence stocks in from the cold [141], and that flow supports the sector’s valuation. In the US, Lockheed Martin is up 5.87% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), a relative bright spot for the sector.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Boeing’s supply problems are sharper than the tariff story. Faulty parts on 787 jets flew below the radar in Italy [142], and AerCap’s chief executive said a 787 could rise $40 million in cost in the worst case [143]. Boeing is down 14.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), while the aerospace and defence ETF is down 4.78% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

Narrative: The consensus is that the US consumer is resilient. The Consumer Discretionary SPDR is at 192.60 USD, down 13.92% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The WSJ says consumer angst is striking all income levels [144], and Dollar General’s chief executive says shoppers only have enough money for basic essentials [145].

Reported: American Eagle said the consumer is slowing and issued weak guidance [146], and Ulta issued weak guidance, citing consumer uncertainty and its own missteps [147]. Dick’s Sporting Goods is the latest retailer to forecast a rocky 2025 [148]. Hugo Boss warned of lingering uncertainty amid weak consumer sentiment [149].

EPS Upside Watch: The upside is in the names with a self-help story. Dick’s 2024 earnings per share rose 15% [150], and its Gamechanger app is adding $100 million of revenue as media ventures grow [151]. Those are the places a surprise can still come from in a sector where the guidance has been cut.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Consumer weakness is being traded as a positive for discount names: Dollar General and Dollar Tree rose as penny-pinching consumers look for low-cost options [152]. Tesla, the most-discussed name in the retail debate, is down 28.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the trade-down is not lifting the discretionary leaders.

Narrative: The consensus is that staples are the defensive shelter. The Consumer Staples SPDR is at 79.33 USD, down 1.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the shelter has held better than the rest of the market. The driver is trade-down: Dollar General warned that American shoppers are struggling [153].

Reported: Dollar General’s sales guidance came in higher than estimates [154], while its store review and closures dented fourth-quarter earnings [155]. Costco stock suffered its biggest one-day drop in over three years [156], and the shares closed at 890.62 USD, down 16.38% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

EPS Upside Watch: The upside case is in discount and value formats, where trade-down spending moves volume [152]. Dollar General’s sales guidance above estimates [154] makes it the clearest upside watch in the group, although its store closures are a cost headwind.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Walmart is down 18.44% over 20 sessions even as trade-down should favour it, and China’s commerce ministry met Walmart over supplier pricing [43]. Walmart closed at 84.50 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the largest US retailer is being squeezed on costs and on pricing.

Narrative: The consensus is that healthcare is defensive growth with a pharma tariff overhang. The Health Care SPDR is at 143.83 USD, down 1.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), a relative shelter. The main driver is obesity drugs: Eli Lilly is down 8.17% over 20 sessions while Merck is up 10.55% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and the Eli Lilly chief executive’s pay reflects the obesity-drug franchise [157].

Reported: Mallinckrodt and Endo’s $6.7 billion merger is getting a bump from tariffs [158], and Ireland could lose its pharma tax advantage to the US after the president’s accusations [159]. Merck opened a billion-dollar US facility to make Gardasil [160], which is a reshoring move in the sector.

EPS Upside Watch: The upside sits with names whose tariff exposure is small and whose franchises are growing. Gilead is a hedge-fund favourite in the pharma group [161], and Vertex is up 10.97% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the defensive bid is working in the large caps.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Hims & Hers, Zealand and Roche fell as weight-loss stocks sold off [162], even as microdosing of weight-loss drugs goes viral and worries experts [163]. Novo Nordisk’s US listing is down 7.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the obesity theme is being sold through the names even as the trend draws attention.

Narrative: The consensus is that materials are a tariff-price story. The Materials SPDR is at 84.87 USD, down 4.23% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), but the metals are rising. Gold closed at 2,991.30 USD, up 2.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and Reuters reports that gold scaled a record high and is sprinting toward $3,000 [164]. Sceptics are active in the sector: PCMag reports scientists question Microsoft’s quantum ‘breakthrough’ [254], and Scientific American argues that scientists, publishers and investors create the hype [255]. The instrument risk is equity supply: IonQ halted its at-the-market programme after a $372 million raise [256], which is the company selling into strength.

Why Retail Is Here: The power story is the newest version of the AI trade. Amazon, Google and Meta support tripling nuclear power by 2050 [173], and World Nuclear News frames the same goal across Amazon, Google, Meta and Dow [257]. Stocktwits reports that NuScale and Oklo surged on the big-tech bet, but retail sentiment pulled back [258]. The crowd’s simple story is that hyperscalers need firm power, and the small-reactor names are the cheapest way to own it. Alphabet’s chief investment officer says Google aims to cut the cost of new nuclear with small reactor deployments [259].

Where It Breaks: Oklo closed at 23.95 USD, down 8.55% in the prior session and 55.96% over 20 sessions, against 54.38 USD on 12 February (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The instrument risk is a low-priced, high-volatility name in a sector where one contract can move the stock.

Robinhood is listing new tokens such as PENGU and POPCAT as crypto activity ramps up [263], and Yahoo reports a new meme coin, Cocoro, launched by Dogecoin’s IP rights holder [264]. The crowd’s story is that the joke is the asset, and the platform that lists the next one wins the attention. Decrypt reports that President Trump’s own Solana meme coin is down 85% from its peak [265], which the crowd reads as the memecoin cycle turning rather than ending.

Where It Breaks: Dogecoin closed at 0.17 USD, down 4.24% in the prior session, 14.11% over five sessions and 31.02% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-13), against 0.24 on 21 February. geo.label: tariff shock / growth scare
parts: Macro Stance

US equities have slipped into correction, and the trigger is tariff policy more than the data. The S&P 500 closed at 5,521.52 index points, down 8.76% over 20 sessions and 3.78% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). CNN framed the day as the Dow sliding and the S&P 500 closing in correction as the trade war escalated [[n11858]]. Goldman Sachs cut its year-end S&P 500 target to 6,200 on weaker profit forecasts [[n3031]], while Citi kept 6,500 as its base case [[n11685]], so the sell-side split is about how much earnings damage tariffs will do, not about the direction of the tape. The growth data are softer than the prices. February CPI came in at 2.8%, under consensus [[n11278]], and payrolls rose 151,000, below expectations [[n10960]]. Powell said the Fed is in no hurry to adjust rates while policy uncertainty runs high [[n11433]]. The VIX closed at 24.66, up 55.19% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and a J.P. Morgan economist puts the US recession odds at 40% [[n0529]].
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.94% and the 10Y at 4.27% (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-13), leaving the 10Y−2Y spread at +33 bps. Over 20 observations the 2Y fell 42 bps and the 10Y fell 35 bps, so the spread widened 7 bps. The curve is positively sloped, and the 20-observation move is bull steepening, with the front end rallying harder than the long end (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-13). The 30Y sits at 4.59%, 24 bps lower over 20 observations, which is a rally led by the policy path rather than a term-premium shock. TLT is up 3.92% over 20 sessions while HYG is down 1.00%, so the bid is in duration rather than credit (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The dollar index stands at 103.83 index points, down 3.81% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the recent dollar decline a natural ‘adjustment’ [[n4051]].
New / Most Important

The most important near-term item is the funding deadline. The New York Times reports that Schumer will clear the way for the Republican spending bill, breaking with his party [[n11891]], and Senate Democrats signalled they will advance the bill to avoid a shutdown [[n11899]]. CNN put the stakes as what is at risk if Congress does not fund the government by Friday [[n11929]]. A shutdown would arrive in the same week the tariff escalation has already pushed the index into correction. CNBC’s argument that markets have learned to ignore shutdowns [[n11876]] is the bull case, but it carries less weight when tariffs are already compressing earnings expectations.
Playbook ✓

Keep duration as the hedge and do not add cyclical equity until the funding vote and the tariff talks clear. Own the long end only while the curve keeps bull steepening, and trim high-beta Nasdaq exposure until the Nasdaq 100 recovers its 20-session reference of 21,719.26 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The call changes if the VIX returns toward its level of 15.89 from 20 sessions earlier and the stopgap clears without a tariff escalation (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

geo.label: fiscal pivot / easing bias
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is easing into a tariff shock with its policy rate already falling. The ECB cut its key rate to 2.5% in early March [[n3354]] and described policy as ‘meaningfully less restrictive’ [[n3356]]. The first risk is that the trade shock hits Germany: the Bundesbank chief said US tariffs could extend Germany’s recession [[n3602]]. The fiscal turn is the offset. Markets rallied when Berlin moved to lift the debt brake for defence and infrastructure [[n3341]], and the shift has been called Germany’s ‘whatever it takes’ moment [[n3387]]. JPMorgan raised its euro-area 2025 growth forecast, joining Goldman [[n3467]]. The DAX is down 0.20% over 20 sessions against 3.13% for the Euro Stoxx 50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the German core is holding up better than the bloc.
Credit & Inflation

Inflation is cooling. Euro-area inflation dipped to 2.4% in February, and the ECB bets point to a sixth rate cut [[n3317]]. Lagarde warned that trade and defence shocks risk amplifying inflation [[n3566]], and that higher defence spending could push it up [[n3559]]. France is the credit pressure point, with borrowing costs near a 14-year high before a Fitch review [[n3584]]. Bund safe-haven status is holding in swaps even as German spending worries mount [[n3503]].
New / Most Important

Trade retaliation has moved from threat to action. The EU will impose counter-tariffs on $28 billion of US goods [[n11761]], and Trump answered with a threatened 200% tariff on European wine after the EU proposed a whiskey tax [[n11914]]. The US trade representative issued a statement on the EU’s retaliatory tariffs [[n11745]]. US importers of EU wine are already warning of closures and layoffs [[n9753]].
Playbook ✓

Own German fiscal beneficiaries on dips, the infrastructure and industrial suppliers that gain from the spending plan, and keep the defence leaders as the cash-flow anchor. Avoid European autos until the tariff path is settled. The call changes if the counter-tariffs are shelved, which would lift autos, or if the Bundesbank’s warning turns into an orders downgrade, which would turn the German overweight into a trim.

geo.label: stimulus vs deflation
parts: Macro Stance

China is trying to hold growth near its target while deflation keeps deepening. The 5% growth goal sets the frame, and South China Morning Post opinion asks where that growth will come from [[n1382]]. The annual Congress closed with questions still open about how to revive a slowing economy [[n1345]]. The stimulus on the table is a $41 billion consumption plan, which CNBC calls just a start as deflationary pressures deepen [[n1196]]. CNN says deflation problems are getting worse [[n1207]], and Bloomberg asks why China cannot escape the cycle [[n1497]]. Policy direction is supportive, but the price data are not confirming it, so the stance is Mixed.
PMIs & Activity

The most recent activity print is February’s non-manufacturing PMI at 50.4, a reading just above the expansion line for services and construction [[n0845]]. That is a positive but thin signal, and it sits against the deflation reading. The view is confirmed if the next non-manufacturing PMI holds above 50 while consumer prices stay in deflation. A drop back below 50 would confirm the bear case that the consumption plan is too small for the demand gap. The index level, not the trend, is the signal today.
Credit Impulse

Credit is the weakest part of the picture, and the evidence is about stress rather than volume. China’s bond yields jumped to three-month highs as investors pared rate-cut expectations [[n1188]]. Evergrande and other units were ordered to repay $1.8 billion of deposit pledges [[n1337]], and some Hong Kong banks are refusing home loans for Vanke’s Le Mont project in Tai Po [[n1394]]. Higher yields with cuts priced out are the opposite of a credit impulse. The read rests on the yield move and the lender retreat, which is enough to keep the credit call negative.
Property

Property is still in adjustment, and policy is steering toward quality over volume. A State Council piece frames the new vision as quality homes amid market adjustment [[n1558]], and analysts warn that the push for better homes adds stress for developers [[n1446]]. A minister says the sector is showing positive changes [[n1155]], which is the official line. Hong Kong’s property slump is pushing hotels toward student housing [[n5387]], a sign of how long the pressure lasts. Turnover is the constraint on any rebound, and the policy direction does not change that in the near term.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Policy is leaning on trade management rather than domestic demand. China’s tariffs on US farm products took effect [[n1442]], and Beijing took issue with the US linking tariffs to fentanyl [[n1515]]. The commerce ministry met Walmart over supplier pricing [[n9436]], a domestic pricing step that shows the government is watching retailers’ costs. A summit between Trump and Xi is being discussed for June [[n1359]], which keeps a negotiation channel open. The fiscal anchor is the 5% growth goal, so the next signal is whether Beijing sizes support above the $41 billion consumption plan [[n1196]].
Markets & Flows

Equities are the bright spot. The Hang Seng closed at 23,462.65 index points, up 7.56% over 20 sessions though down 0.58% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The Shanghai Composite is at 3,358.73 index points, up 0.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Hong Kong’s market has been booming while Wall Street is in turmoil [[n11869]], and ADR premiums for Chinese names are widening as the stock rerating continues [[n1526]]. The China large-cap ETF (FXI) is up 7.08% over 20 sessions and the internet ETF (KWEB) is up 5.87% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Chinese stocks and emerging-market debt drew large inflows in February [[n1528]], and mainland investors bought a record amount of Hong Kong stocks to play AI [[n1243]]. The currency is firmer: USD/CNY closed at 7.2371, down 0.98% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and the offshore yuan climbed to a four-month high [[n1477]].
New / Most Important

The new signal is the gap between the stimulus size and the deflation problem. The $41 billion consumption plan [[n1196]] sits beside a 5% growth goal, and the market is reading it as a start rather than a fix. The equity leg is being carried by AI. Alibaba released an AI model that reads emotions to take on OpenAI [[n1421]], and its chairman Joe Tsai argues that consumers’ $20 trillion of savings is the growth lever China needs [[n1447]]. The next change to the view comes from policy. If Beijing extends consumption support beyond this plan, the deflation read improves; if it does not, the equity rally runs ahead of the economy.
Playbook ✓

Own the equity beta in Hong Kong internet and AI names on dips, keep duration neutral, and avoid property developers until the credit data confirm a turn. Keep yuan exposure small above the four-month high. The call changes if the consumption plan is extended and the PMI holds above 50. ⚠ Divergence: the Hang Seng is up 7.56% over 20 sessions while the credit and property reads are still negative (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

geo.label: BOJ hike bias / tariff drag
parts: Macro Stance

Japan’s rate path is tightening into a weak growth patch. The 10-year yield reached its highest level since 2008 on bets for BOJ hikes [[n5305]], and Reuters reports that a rate-hike discussion could come in May if inflation risks persist [[n5238]]. Growth is softer: the economy downgraded its fourth-quarter GDP [[n5308]], and services sentiment soured on the cost of living [[n5310]]. Wages are the reason the BOJ leans hawkish. Major firms agreed large pay increases [[n5398]], and the largest union group sought its biggest wage increase in over 30 years [[n5240]]. The Nikkei 225 sits at 36,790.03 index points, down 5.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Activity & Currency

USD/JPY closed at 148.2790, down 3.87% over 20 sessions, which means the yen has strengthened against the dollar (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The yen is also being bid as a haven: one strategist calls it the new safe-haven currency [[n5272]], while Kuroda warned that Japan must fix the impression that it manipulates the yen [[n5254]]. The tariff track is unhelpful. Japan’s trade minister did not win a tariff exemption assurance [[n5311]], and the prime minister’s gifts apology clouded the budget outlook [[n5421]]. Toyota is down 2.89% over 20 sessions and Sony is up 3.47% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so exporter shares are not moving as one.
Playbook ✓

Favour banks and domestic wage beneficiaries over exporters while the BOJ path is live, and use yen longs as the hedge for exporter exposure. Avoid adding long-duration JGBs at 2008-high yields until the May discussion is clearer. The call changes if the tariff talks produce a concrete exemption or if the yen reverses above its 20-session reference of 154.2550 (2025-02-13).

geo.label: cuts done / iron ore drag
parts: Macro Stance

Australia’s growth is turning up from a low base. The economy exited a 21-month per capita recession [[n0157]], and Bloomberg reports that growth accelerated, which backs the RBA’s hawkish tone [[n0159]]. The RBA cut in February [[n0075]], and the governor has played down the chance of more cuts [[n0073]]. Tariffs are the drag. Albanese called US tariffs ‘not a friendly act’ [[n0333]], and Trump has said Australia’s hope of an exemption is fading [[n1289]]. Canberra says it will not retaliate [[n11747]].
Demand & Financing

AUD/USD closed at 0.6328, up 0.71% over 20 sessions, so the currency is holding up despite the tariff noise (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The ASX 200 is at 7,749.10 index points, down 9.26% over 20 sessions and 4.27% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). BlackRock cut its exposure to Australian shares on value grounds [[n0260]], and the iron ore chain is under pressure from China’s steel cuts [[n0251]]. BHP is down 6.71% over 20 sessions and Fortescue 19.38% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The central bank has also raised concern about banks’ plan to shut a key payments system [[n0428]].
Playbook ✓

Hold the miners on pullbacks only while iron ore holds, underweight the banks against the ASX 200’s drawdown, and keep the AUD long as the tariff hedge. The call flips if China’s steel cuts reverse and the miners lead the index back up. A break in the Australian dollar’s own trend would change the currency view, not the equity one.

geo.label: hold / strong zloty
parts: Macro Stance

The Polish economy is turning up. The manufacturing PMI signalled a recovery in industry and an end to a nearly three-year recession [[n5785]]. The central bank governor, Glapiński, said there are no reasons to cut rates now [[n5581]], and said the fall in inflation is still a ‘dość odległy horyzont’, a distant horizon [[n6126]]. The rate path is therefore a hold. Parkiet argues it is not the time for emotion around the monetary council, the RPP [[n6076]], while Business Insider Polska frames the next decision as relief for borrowers arriving [[n6055]]. The labour data conflict. Eurostat put Poland at a record-low unemployment rate, joint-lowest in the EU [[n10792]], while the labour ministry explains a rise in unemployment [[n5975]], so the labour market gets no directional call. Official wage data are positive, with GUS reporting 2024 pay figures that show higher earnings [[n5786]].
Markets

The zloty is the strongest asset in the block. USD/PLN closed at 3.8452, down 3.93% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.1838 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The euro was at its cheapest against the zloty since 2018 [[n5777]], and Bloomberg reported that the zloty surged to a 10-year high on a hawkish central bank [[n5467]]. The governor also made an unambiguous statement on whether the central bank would intervene in the currency [[n6120]]. Equities are following. The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 50.96 PLN, up 3.44% over 20 sessions, and the iShares MSCI Poland ETF at 27.58 USD, up 7.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Orlen is up 16.10% over 20 sessions and PKO 3.50% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy is leaning toward defence. EU ministers backed a temporary exemption for defence spending from the EU’s budget rules [[n5531]], and a Credit Agricole economist says the Union is moving toward looser fiscal rules [[n6010]]. The VAT gap fell unexpectedly last year, which helps the budget arithmetic [[n6074]]. Politically, the far-right candidate has moved into second place in the presidential race [[n5515]], and Biejat, who says she would tidy up the mortgage market as president, is pitching on housing [[n5905]]. The US has said it will retaliate if Poland introduces a tax on big tech [[n5527]].
Corporate & Sectors

Corporate news is strong, and buybacks are the common thread. Allegro expects 2025 earnings growth and proposed a $364 million buyback [[n5576]], and the Polish press reports double-digit profit growth, with the company saying it has proved it can deliver [[n6115]]. Allegro closed at 32.38 PLN, up 13.61% in the prior session and 11.02% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). PKO BP’s results show Poland’s largest bank boasting a profit jump of almost 4 billion zloty [[n6136]], and a record dividend is being discussed [[n6145]]; the shares closed at 74.02 PLN, up 3.32% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Orlen still lacks a final agreement with Sołowow on the small-nuclear project [[n6140]], yet Orlen is up 16.10% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Dino Polska is hiring 1,300 people [[n6122]] and its shares are at a record high [[n5823]]. KGHM’s chief executive says years of neglect and no investment are the problem [[n5868]], and the stock is down 2.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Geopolitics & Security

Security is the louder narrative. Polish President Duda urged the US to move nuclear warheads onto Polish territory, the FT reported [[n5584]], and told the BBC that US nuclear weapons in Poland would be a deterrent for Russia [[n5572]]. Warsaw wants 100,000 volunteers for military training in 2027 [[n5546]] and has asked NATO to raise the minimum defence spending to 3% of GDP [[n5485]]. Prosecutors say Russia used a spy posing as a Belarusian refugee to set a Warsaw mall on fire [[n5565]]. Washington’s line is blunter: Rubio told Poland to ‘say thank you’ amid the Starlink spat over Ukraine [[n5504]].
New / Most Important

The one signal that matters is that defence is now both a budget and a currency story. The EU’s temporary carve-out [[n5531]] and the 3% NATO request [[n5485]] turn defence into a multi-year fiscal commitment. Speculative equity money is following: Bankier reports that steel and armaments names have taken over speculative attention on the Warsaw exchange [[n5977]], and a separate Bankier piece says the defence sector is trading on the military rally [[n5840]]. For investors the meaning is that the Polish equity move increasingly depends on military budgets rather than on the consumer.
Playbook ✓

Own the zloty winners with dividend and buyback support, PKO and Allegro, and keep the defence names as a tactical trade rather than a core holding. Hedge a zloty long against a surprise shift in the central bank’s tone, even though the governor has ruled out reasons to cut for now. The call changes if USD/PLN climbs back above its reference of 4.0026 from 13 February (Yahoo Finance). ⚠ Divergence: the WIG20 tracker is up 3.44% over 20 sessions while KGHM is down 2.75% over the same period (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Narrative

The consensus says AI demand keeps technology earnings compounding, while the 20-session tape says the market is repricing monetisation. The Technology Select Sector SPDR is at 207.66 USD, down 11.94% over 20 sessions and 1.90% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The driver that matters now is whether software and AI spending can show revenue, not just usage, and Reuters reports that Adobe’s dull forecast raised AI monetisation doubts [[n3006]].
Reported

Adobe beat on its first quarter, but its revenue outlook disappointed and the stock fell [[n3106]]. CNBC put the drop at 14% as concerns about AI growth overshadowed the beat [[n3109]], and Adobe is down 13.85% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Oracle’s sales missed estimates even as its chief executive pointed to AI-driven growth [[n0492]]. Workday’s full-year EPS missed expectations [[n3183]].
EPS Upside Watch

The set-up for a surprise is in AI infrastructure rather than application software. ServiceNow agreed a record $2.9 billion deal for Moveworks [[n6339]], and Broadcom’s call highlighted record revenue and AI growth [[n2684]]. Suppliers are lining up announcements for the 2025 Nvidia GTC conference [[n9560]], which gives the chain a pending showcase.

The consensus is that ad-supported platforms and streaming keep growing. The Communication Services SPDR is at 94.84 USD, down 8.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Meta is the swing name, down 18.58% over 20 sessions and 4.67% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Ad budgets are under pressure too: Sirius XM fell 8.6% as its ad sales collapsed [[n11174]].
Reported

Telecoms flagged softness, and Verizon and AT&T shares slid after both signalled near-term weakness [[n6471]]. Netflix is down 13.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Meta is launching Community Notes in the US [[n9584]], a product step rather than a reported result.
EPS Upside Watch

The upside lever is creator monetisation. Facebook now lets creators get paid for views on stories [[n3138]], which adds revenue at the margin, though it is small against the ad-budget squeeze. Spotify’s $10 billion payment to the music industry shows the royalty cost base is rising [[n3070]], which limits the streaming upside.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Telecom is the exception to the sector’s weakness. Verizon is up 7.85% and AT&T 2.88% over 20 sessions while the sector ETF is down 8.35% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the defensive bid is working inside a sector that is supposed to be growth.

The consensus is that banks are cheap on capital return. The Financial Select SPDR is at 47.42 USD, down 7.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The driver is recession pricing and credit: US corporate bond spreads hit their widest in about six months on recession fears [[n3950]], and Goldman Sachs says spreads will get a lot wider amid tariffs [[n3916]]. JPMorgan is down 18.25% over 20 sessions and Goldman Sachs 19.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Reported

Bank stocks tumbled as recession fears rose [[n0508]], and Citigroup, Goldman Sachs and SoFi were hit hardest in the Monday sell-off [[n6272]]. Bank of America cut 150 junior investment-banking jobs [[n11210]], a cost signal rather than a loss signal. Goldman’s 2024 results beat expectations [[n2213]], an older print that still anchors the group’s earnings base.
EPS Upside Watch

The upside case rests on cost discipline and trading. Bank of America’s cuts [[n11210]] and the Stifel regulatory fine [[n9711]] show the group trimming costs, and the volatility of the tariff tape is the usual driver of trading desks’ revenue, so a surprise would come from trading activity.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Berkshire Hathaway is up 6.89% over 20 sessions while the sector falls (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and Warren Buffett’s ‘keep your head’ advice in a falling market reached a wide audience [[n11599]]. Berkshire is acting as the shelter in this tape.

The consensus is that OPEC+ supply and softer demand keep crude range-bound. WTI closed at 66.55 USD, down 6.75% over 20 sessions, while the energy ETF is up 1.42% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The IEA’s March oil market report is the demand reference [[n9634]], and oil settled lower on tariff worry and supply-demand expectations [[n9638]].
Reported

Record OPEC+ fuel exports blunt the group’s crude supply cut [[n9676]], which caps the price upside. The upside case is in gas: Henry Hub closed at 4.11 USD, up 15.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and AI and LNG demand are expected to keep US gas use at record highs [[n9357]].

The WSJ says consumer angst is striking all income levels [[n9448]], and Dollar General’s chief executive says shoppers only have enough money for basic essentials [[n3989]].

Dick’s Sporting Goods is the latest retailer to forecast a rocky 2025 [[n0502]]. Hugo Boss warned of lingering uncertainty amid weak consumer sentiment [[n11340]].
